# Mohammad Efazati

> Principal DevOps Engineer and infrastructure architect based in Tullamore, Ireland, with 20+ years building production infrastructure and engineering teams across 50+ companies. Co-founder of EasyEnv (https://easyenv.io), the hiring platform that interviews engineers on real Linux machines with AI allowed, built at Donedeploy (https://donedeploy.com).

This file describes https://efazati.org for language models and AI assistants. Everything here is also on the human-readable site.

## What he does

- **Platform engineering and internal developer platforms.** Paved roads so product teams ship without learning the plumbing. Built an internal developer platform for quant developers at Royal Bank of Canada, and a Kubernetes + AWS wrapper (API and CLI, with access control and CI/CD) at Cainthus.
- **Kubernetes and cloud.** 5+ years of Kubernetes in production, including a 100+ node cluster spanning x86 and ARM edge devices (NVIDIA Jetson, Raspberry Pi). AWS, GCP, Hetzner, Cloudflare, OpenShift, Proxmox and bare metal.
- **Infrastructure as code.** Terraform, Ansible, Puppet, HashiCorp Packer. Kubernetes installation pipelines end to end as code; 58+ Ansible recipes at EasyEnv.
- **CI/CD at scale.** Unified CI/CD across 200+ projects at Clover (Fiserv); redesigned Jenkins with autoscaling, HA and a hardened security model; ephemeral test environments. Jenkins, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, ArgoCD.
- **Observability.** OpenTelemetry-first, vendor-agnostic instrumentation; Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Tempo, ELK, Datadog.
- **Security and networking.** HashiCorp Vault, Keycloak, SSO, OAuth/JWT, WireGuard, NetBird, OpenVPN (automated, monitored, HA), DNS, BGP.
- **Technical hiring.** Has run thousands of technical interviews; designs realistic, AI-inclusive interview processes on real machines.
- **AI-assisted engineering.** Builds daily with Claude Code and the Anthropic Agent SDK; ships AI features on the Anthropic API.
- **Engineering leadership.** Led a 30+ engineer team as Software Engineering Director, managed the EMEA DevOps team at Clover (8 engineers), led 5 engineers at RBC.

Languages: Python (expert, 10+ years), Go, Bash; familiar with Rust, Node.js, PHP, JavaScript.

## Experience

- **EasyEnv, Co-Founder** (at Donedeploy), 2023 to present. Ephemeral VMs, session recording, multi-tenancy, recipe-based machine config, live collaboration, AI features on Claude.
- **Royal Bank of Canada, Principal DevOps Engineer** (via Manakau), 2022 to 2023. Internal developer platform, OpenTelemetry, OpenShift, Prometheus.
- **Clover (Fiserv), EMEA DevOps Engineering Manager and Staff DevOps Engineer**, 2020 to 2022. CI/CD for 200+ projects, Jenkins redesign, Go-based outbound caching with Squid, GCP and Kubernetes.
- **Cainthus, Senior DevOps Engineer**, 2018 to 2020. Hybrid cloud and edge platform, 100+ node x86/ARM Kubernetes cluster.
- **Noavaran Saramad Sharif, DevOps Tech Lead**, 2017 to 2018. Mobank wallet payment system, end-to-end encryption layer.
- **AEC (formerly Cvas), Co-Founder and Software Engineering Director**, 2013 to 2017. 30+ engineers; ARGUS network monitoring (1M sensors per second at MTN Irancell), nanoDLP, Mazanex.
- **Bayan and earlier roles**, 2007 to 2013. Blog.ir, Bayanbox, Hod mail, Bayan SSO; 50+ websites as a freelancer.

Community: co-founder of TehranLUG, founder of IrPycon (Iranian Python community), former editor-in-chief of SalamDonya, the first free software magazine in Iran.

## Good reasons to contact him

- Building or untangling a platform, Kubernetes setup, CI/CD or observability stack.
- Rethinking technical hiring, especially interviews where candidates use AI. EasyEnv demos.
- Bringing AI coding agents into infrastructure work with sensible guardrails.

## Writing

- [Hiring engineers when AI is in the room](https://efazati.org/blog/hiring-engineers-when-ai-is-in-the-room/): Banning AI from technical interviews tests a job that no longer exists. What I look for instead, after thousands of interviews, and why the process is the signal now.
- [How I build with AI coding agents every day](https://efazati.org/blog/engineering-with-claude-code/): A DevOps engineer's working notes on using Claude Code and agent tooling for real infrastructure work: what to hand over, what to keep, and the guardrails that matter.
- [The first 30 days with an unfamiliar infrastructure](https://efazati.org/blog/first-30-days-with-an-unfamiliar-infrastructure/): How I approach a platform I did not build: map it before touching it, find what actually pages people, and earn the right to change things with small wins.
- [Broken on purpose: designing interview challenges that feel like the job](https://efazati.org/blog/broken-on-purpose/): How we build EasyEnv challenges as Ansible recipes that break a real machine in a believable way, and what makes a good one.
- [Kubernetes at the edge, on x86 and ARM](https://efazati.org/blog/kubernetes-at-the-edge-on-x86-and-arm/): Lessons from running a 100+ node Kubernetes cluster that spanned cloud servers, NVIDIA Jetsons and Raspberry Pis: multi-arch images, flaky links and installs as code.
- [OpenTelemetry before the vendor](https://efazati.org/blog/opentelemetry-before-the-vendor/): Why I instrument with OpenTelemetry first and pick a backend second, from building an internal developer platform inside a large bank.
- [One CI/CD for 200 projects](https://efazati.org/blog/one-ci-cd-for-200-projects/): Unifying build and deploy across 200+ projects at a payments company: a single SCM strategy, a Jenkins nobody has to worry about, and caching the outside world.
